s: a stripped-back Praga coffee roastery-cafe with an unusually deep tea list too
w: A minimalist roastery-cafe on Kłopotowskiego where the focus stays entirely on the cup -- single-origin beans from Ethiopia, Rwanda, Kenya and Yemen brewed by aeropress, siphon, chemex or drip, alongside an equally serious tea selection. Little in the way of scene or seating theatrics; people come specifically for the brew.
_facts: Located at ul. Księdza Ignacego Kłopotowskiego 23/25, Praga-Północ, Warszawa
Operates as both a coffee roastery and cafe, plus an online/retail shop
Offers single-origin coffees brewed by multiple methods (aeropress, siphon, chemex, drip)
Also stocks an extensive tea selection

s: a relaxed Saska Kępa cafe pairing specialty coffee with a wall of records
w: A neighbourhood cafe on the leafy Praga side of the river, in Saska Kępa, that pairs well-made specialty coffee with a vinyl collection and easygoing, unhurried energy. Works equally as a daytime coffee stop or a place to linger over a record.
_facts: Located at Elsterska 10, 03-907 Warszawa, Saska Kępa
Combines a specialty coffee bar with a vinyl records theme/collection
Situated in Saska Kępa, a quiet, leafy residential district on Warsaw's Praga side

s: a gloriously mismatched flea-market bar near Dworzec Wileński
w: A multi-room bar on Ząbkowska stuffed with flea-market furniture, clashing colours and eccentric bric-a-brac -- the kind of studied chaos that has made it a fixture of Praga's bohemian nightlife for years. Craft beer, a young artsy crowd, and an atmosphere that feels genuinely lived-in rather than styled for visitors.
_facts: Located at ul. Ząbkowska 6, 03-735 Warszawa, Praga-Północ
Long-running bar known for its mismatched vintage/flea-market furniture and decor
A short walk from Dworzec Wileński metro station
Popular with students and Praga's artistic/bohemian crowd

s: a vodka museum inside the rectification building of a 19th-century distillery, now a creative complex
w: Housed in the original rectification building of the 19th-century Koneser vodka factory -- once producer of the Luksusowa and Wyborowa brands -- this is the world's only museum dedicated to Polish vodka's 500-year history. The wider Koneser complex around it has been reborn as a mixed-use hub of bars, restaurants and event spaces inside the old neo-Gothic factory buildings.
_facts: Located at Plac Konesera 1, 03-736 Warszawa, Praga-Północ
Opened June 2018 inside the historic rectification building of the former Koneser vodka distillery
Only museum in the world dedicated specifically to the 500-year history of Polish vodka
Part of the wider Centrum Praskie Koneser complex, a reused 19th-century neo-Gothic industrial site now housing bars, restaurants and cultural venues
